_comment: Columns a LitRPG or progression-fantasy bible needs that a general novel bible does not. Read by the pack applier (EntitySchema.applyPack); the binary carries a frozen _fallback_only copy in BibleDemoSeed for the demo only. Applying a pack ADDS a view — it never widens Essentials, so a three-character short story that installs this by accident sees no change to its default columns. DECODER SAFETY: comment keys at this TOP LEVEL ONLY; every field object is fixed-field. NAMING: these are deliberately NOT D&D attribute names. The machinery is genre-neutral (NumericLedgerEntry over any .number field marked isTimeVarying) and the vocabulary is content — which is the whole point. A pack author renaming Clarity to Intelligence changes one string here and ships in seconds. matchesPackKey is how an upgrade finds an existing column: never the display name, which the author may have renamed, and never the FieldID.
_fieldNotes: promptTier: always = injected every call (spend it carefully); whenRelevant = injected when the entity is retrieved; onDemand = fetchable by tool only. isTimeVarying: true routes writes to the numeric ledger rather than the entity's property map, which is what makes 'as of chapter N' answerable. aiVisible: false keeps a column out of prompts entirely — use it for anything the model would over-repeat.

character.name: Class
character.llmHint: Named by the System at first delve. Changing it is a plot event, not a preference.

character.name: Tier
character.llmHint: Non-decreasing. A crawler never loses a tier.

character.name: Grit
character.llmHint: Endurance. Falls with untreated injury and does not self-heal.

character.name: Standing
character.llmHint: Bureaucratic favour. CAN GO NEGATIVE; negative Standing is a plot state, not a debuff.

character.name: Affiliation
character.llmHint: Time-varying on purpose: who someone answers to in chapter 40 is rarely who they answered to in chapter 3.

character.name: Known Debts
character.llmHint: Obligations the System can call in. Plot fuel — fetch when the scene turns on leverage.

item.name: Rule Text
item.llmHint: The item's stated behaviour. Treat as an ENFORCEABLE CONSTRAINT, not flavour — a returning sword that was defined well enough to become a plot constraint has to behave like one.

item.name: Modifier
item.llmHint: e.g. '+4 Grit while worn'. Record the CONDITION — a modifier that only applies sometimes is the single most common source of stat drift.

item.name: Held By
item.llmHint: Time-varying: possession changes, and 'who had it in chapter 12' is a real question.

faction.name: Standing With Party
faction.llmHint: Tracks across the whole book. A faction's opinion is exactly the kind of number authors lose track of.

floor.name: Floor Rule
floor.llmHint: The rule that governs this floor. Always-tier because breaking it silently is the failure readers notice first.
